_doc: Maps calculator asset-class keys (broker_ibkr.json keys) to harness instrument selectors. Two forms are accepted. (1) A LIST of instrument-key patterns, matched against `_instrument_key(df)` from quality/analyze.py, which produces '<symbol>/<secType>' or '<symbol>/<secType>/<expiry>'; '*' is an fnmatch wildcard. (2) An OBJECT with any of `patterns`, `exchange_any`, `currency_any` — every key present must hold. Form 2 exists because the EU classes partition by VENUE and the instrument key carries no venue; see `_venue_partitioned`.
_venue_partitioned: EU_STK_XETRA, EU_STK_LSE and EU_STK_SIX are the same secType on three
different venues. `_instrument_key` is '<symbol>/<secType>', so it cannot
tell them apart and a symbol-only pattern for one would match a listing on
either of the others. Hence `exchange_any` / `currency_any`, matched against
the trial row's own `exchange` and `currency` — the contract IBKR resolved,
⚑ THE PATTERNS ARE DELIBERATELY BROAD ('*/STK'). The venue defines these
buckets; the symbol is whatever local ticker the venue lists the fund under,
and NOTHING in this workspace records that mapping — the universe screen's
`venues` column is null on all 1,851 rows. A guessed ticker here would give a
bucket that silently matches nothing, which is the exact failure this file was
⚑ SMART IS NOT AN ACCEPTED EXCHANGE FOR THESE THREE. A SMART-routed order
records `exchange = SMART`, so the row could not say which venue it measured —
and measuring the router is not measuring the venue. `runner.py` builds the EU
contracts on the explicit venue for that reason. IBKR codes: XETRA = IBIS
(IBIS2 for the second gateway), LSE = LSE, SIX = EBS.
